The figure is a bar chart illustrating the percentage of respondents who believe certain measures could limit “hidden economics” within a country. The horizontal axis represents categories of measures, with labels ranging from “Da se sili граничния контрол” (To enforce border control) to “Da se namali ДДС” (To reduce VAT). The vertical axis represents the percentage of respondents, ranging from 0% to 20%, with increments of 2%. Each bar corresponds to a specific measure, and the height of each bar indicates the percentage of respondents who support that measure. The bars are arranged in a left-to-right order, following the sequence of the labels on the horizontal axis. The tallest bar represents “Да се подобри качеството на административните…” (To improve the quality of administrative…), reaching 13%, followed by “Да се насили ефективния стимул за бизнеса” (To implement effective business incentives) at 9%.  The shortest bars are “Да се ограничи действанията на мафията” (To limit the activities of the mafia) and “Да се вьедат по-ефективни начала акции” (To introduce post-strict laws), both at 5%.  The colors of the bars are consistent throughout the chart, with each bar having a distinct color.

The vertical axis represents the percentage of respondents, ranging from 0% to 20% in increments of 2%, with the scale labeled in whole numbers. The bars are arranged in a left-to-right order corresponding to the order of the measures listed on the horizontal axis.
